items.title: Stronger August Core Inflation, But Details Are Disinflationary
items.summary: Rounded 0.3% month-over-month core CPI is probably just enough for a September Fed hike. But details support further disinflation and cooler upcoming core inflation readings. That suggests an October “hold” awaiting more data and, if core inflation remains cooler, another hold in December.

items.title: Global Macro Strategy: Worries and Game Changers
items.summary: We're often asked if we're worried about a structurally hawkish FOMC, global long end rates, the big Japan carry unwind, oil and TTF. We discuss why we're more sanguine about these, as well as our bigger, more simple concerns: a very strong core CPI print and AI risks from model bans.

items.title: Global FX Strategy: Geopolitical Risks Are Rising for EUR
items.summary: We think Thursday’s repricing across G10 was more about energy than hawkish ECB guidance or U.S. PPI data. We're watching the Euribor curve for indications of when the market might treat a hawkish ECB as a policy error. We offer further analysis in this note.

items.title: PULSE Monitor: Remembrance
items.summary: I remember the confusion, realization and horror as 9/11 unfolded; 25 years later, its butterfly effects continue. Yet the American ethos remains, with Wall Street reflecting our free enterprise system's adaptability. "Change is the only constant" is particularly true in equity markets.

items.title: Where Are We Now in European Defense?
items.summary: We think European defense names' derating offers significant upside for much of the sector. We review concerns we've heard from investors in this note. Our top picks are Babcock (60% upside), followed by Leonardo, RENK, Rheinmetall, and Thales (39-52% upside).

items.title: U.S. Beverages/Household & Personal Care: Second-Half Thoughts
items.summary: In considering the year's second half, at a sector level we continue to prefer the Household/Personal Care and non-alcoholic beverage sectors to alcohol. Our top picks remain skewed to these categories, with CL top overall pick, followed by KO, KDP, and PG.

items.title: Global TMT Conference Takeaways: North America Transportation
items.summary: We hosted FDX, CHRW, and RXO at our Global TMT Conference to discuss how technology is transforming supply chains and driving efficiencies across transports. We note certain common themes from the three companies, with this note offering a more in-depth look at our key takeaways.

items.title: Global TMT Conference Day 3: U.S. Industrial Conglomerates
items.summary: Day 3 of our Global TMT Conference brought discussion of grid/power availability continuing to be a key constraint with behind-the-meter solutions being increasingly recognized following Texas Batch Zero, and software companies integrating AI to deepen competitive moats.

items.title: Global TMT Conference Day 3: Key Takeaways for Semis
items.summary: Day 3 of our Global TMT Conference included fireside chats that we hosted with AEIS and Tokyo Electron, as well as meetings with VECO, CLS, Advantest and Lasertec. We explore key takeaways in this note.

items.title: Global TMT Conference: Key Takeaways for European Media
items.summary: We summarize key takeaways and notes for European media from our Global TMT Conference in New York. We hosted Publicis and WPP and met a number of interesting private companies, including Legora and Perplexity.

items.title: European Rates Weekly: Doing What Needs to Be Done
items.summary: Further ECB rate hikes seem the most logical scenario if risks around energy supply don’t subside, raising the chance of "insurance" hike pricing becoming crystallized. Gamma has finally woken up, and we recommend chasing it higher by buying right-hand skew on the € front end.

items.title: European Equities and the Natural Gas Price Shock
items.summary: European natural gas prices have reached their highest level since late 2022, and a continued rise, amid escalating geopolitical tensions, would pose growing risks to European equities. But as we explore herein, equities appear less sensitive to gas prices than during 2022's energy shock.

items.title: ECB: Higher for Longer
items.summary: Given the explanation for the ECB's 25-basis-point hike, we now expect additional such hikes in December and March, provided energy prices stay high. We explain why we think the ECB's policy horizon has shortened, with its policy preferences drifting toward a “risk management” approach.

items.title: Off the Cuff: The Temperature is Rising!
items.summary: Several market topics have been the focus of nearly every client conversation of late. We review our U.S. equities views in light of five oft-heard questions, ranging from the Fed's circumstances post-Jackson Hole to whether our year-end 8100 target now looks aggressive.

items.title: Must C: Latin America Is Poised for Takeoff
items.summary: Latin America is entering one of its most favorable environments in years, with both external and domestic conditions supporting a potential acceleration in growth. We see the opportunity as significant, but think lasting success will depend on reforms, execution, and policy consistency.

items.title: Australia Economics: We Now Expect Two More 2026 Rate Hikes
items.summary: We now expect Australia to raise rates twice more this year. This view is driven by a two-speed economy, where a deepening housing correction is offset by an AI-related investment boom that is adding to capacity constraints. We push our first rate-cut forecast out to 2027's fourth quarter.

items.title: Biopharma Back to School Summit Day 2: U.S. Biotechnology
items.summary: Day 2 kicked off with policy expert Tommy Barletta reinforcing a manageable outlook for Biopharma heading into the midterms. Political noise may increase, but we see limited risk of near-term changes to Biopharma fundamentals. We offer company specifics and further analysis in this note.

items.title: Emerging Markets Strategy Weekly: Resilience Amid Vulnerabilities
items.summary: Emerging markets remain resilient to macro volatility, as strong inflows suggest investors remain comfortable holding EM risk. The main challenge lies in global rates rather than EM fundamentals, as continued volatility in long-end U.S. Treasury yields could test the durability of inflows.

items.title: U.S. Economics: August's Labor Market Update
items.summary: August employment data were stronger than we expected, with residual seasonal patterns not leading to the rise in the unemployment rate we had anticipated. Despite some cautions, we think the still-stable labor market is unlikely to drive inflationary pressure in the coming months.

items.title: Global TMT Conference Day 2: VC Panel Insights
items.summary: Our software venture-capital panel highlighted a shift to company-specific investments focused on retention, differentiated AI harnesses and durable workflow ownership. Panelists were most constructive on vertical AI and workflow automation. We offer more takeaways in this note.

items.title: Global TMT Conference Day 2: U.S. Semis & Semiconductor Equipment
items.summary: We hosted fireside chats with OLED, INFQ and FORM; met with TXN, MPWR, AVT, TER and MKSI; and hosted EDA and Quantum panels. We offer key takeaways from Day 2 of our Global TMT Conference in this note.

items.title: Global TMT Conference Day 2: U.S. Industrial Conglomerates
items.summary: Day 2 discussions continued to point to broad investment across data, digitization, and power infrastructure, which we see supporting a demand for several industrial end markets. We see growing tailwinds from Physical AI and factory automation investments lifting automation-exposed names.

items.title: Global TMT Conference Day 2: U.S. Electric Utilities
items.summary: Day 2 of our Global TMT Conference spotlighted that data-center developers are adapting to the reality of power market constraints for the next few years, AI labs are looking to improve efficiency of compute, and the data-center industry sees longer-term power demand remaining a wild card.

items.title: Biopharma Back to School Summit Day 1: U.S. Biotechnoogy
items.summary: We hosted LXRX, SPTX, ZBIO, and ZYME for investor-facing conversations during Day 1 of our Biopharma Back to School Summit. In this note we offer takeaways from our afternoon sessions, organized in alphabetical order by ticker.

items.title: Correlation Corner: #9: Looking for U.S.-Iran Hedges
items.summary: Cross-asset correlations have yet to normalize to pre-conflict levels as the oil shock remains stickier than expected. In contrast, we see European equity/oil and equity/yield implied correlations have started to price a meaningful de-escalation scenario. We explore tactics in this note.

items.title: Global Theme Machine: Momentum and Quality Reshape Leaderboard
items.summary: The Theme Model delivered a positive return in August. Ranking changes were driven by a combination of earnings momentum recovery and quality improvement in healthcare themes, alongside a continuation of price-momentum leadership in financials and industrials.

items.title: What 2021-23 Changed in Turkey, and What Comes Next
items.summary: We think Turkey’s 2021-23 macro episode reshaped how the economy earns, saves and spends, with these changes now central to both the growth outlook and the prospects for disinflation. We analyze this structural transformation: where it came from, how far it has run, and what it might mean.

items.title: Global FX Strategy: U.S. Inflation Matters More for USD
items.summary: An ECB rate hike is already well priced by markets, setting the bar high for a material EURUSD move. If anything, U.S. inflation data will be the bigger driver for FX. We expect benign data, allowing markets to remove some of the hawkish premium in the curve.

items.title: Global TMT Conference Day 1: Data-Center Industry Implications
items.summary: Overall data-center demand indicators remain positive, with supply still constrained in many markets. We think firms with an energized power pipeline can capture favorable leasing for at least the next six to 12 months. We review our preferences and offer takeaways in this note.

items.title: Global TMT Conference Day 1: U.S. Industrial Conglomerates
items.summary: We offer takeaways from Day 1 of our Global TMT Conference Day for multi-industrial and E&C names we cover. We came away incrementally more positive on the data-center infrastructure buildout given increasingly demonstrable AI productivity outcomes. We offer more analysis in this note.

items.title: The Missing Driver in the Commercial Aftermarket? Airline Margins
items.summary: We know after-market profits are heavily influenced by airline flight-hours, but our analysis suggests airline margins may be a better predictor of total shareholder return. We look at how this plays out for Safran, MTU and Rolls Royce, with further takeaways in this note.

items.title: China IT Services and Software: AI Inflecting, Divergence Widens
items.summary: We began to upgrade some China IT services/software names in the second quarter due to a host of factors, discussed herein. The sector is showing bifurcation, with AI-driven names delivering strong momentum even as legacy software and property-related verticals continue to disappoint.

items.title: China Economics: Supply Shocks Drive Another Inflationary Impulse
items.summary: China's CPI and PPI rebounded in August, driven almost entirely by supply shocks, as domestic demand remains sluggish. We stay cautious about the inflation outlook and will be watching policy deployment closely. Meanwhile, policy actions have accelerated meaningfully as September unfolds.

items.title: Back to School: Constructive on Broadening, Alert to Risks
items.summary: Global equities have traded sideways of late as markets weigh competing forces likely to shape the path to year's end. While solid fundamentals should underpin continued gains for global equities through mid-2027, we acknowledge that risks around equities are more finely balanced.

items.title: The UK's New Productivity Puzzle and the AI Structural Shift
items.summary: UK productivity growth is finally on the rise after years of poor performance. We see Information & Communication Technology as the primary driver, with some help from other sectors that benefit from AI. We think this development is both positive and meaningful, though we remain cautious.

items.title: U.S. Semiconductors and Semiconductor Equipment: Earnings Recap
items.summary: SOX saw an 18% summer selloff amid high expectations and decelerating earnings momentum, but we expect a rebound, with positive commentary at our Global TMT conference. Data-center demand remains strong and auto/industrial continues to recover, but demand from PCs/handsets remains weak.

items.title: European Capital Goods: The Broadening Theme Gains Momentum
items.summary: Our top picks for the second half include Legrand, Daimler Truck, Atlas Copco, Epiroc, KION, Halma, Nordex, Weir, and Wartsila. We've upgraded KION and Nordex to Buy, and opened positive catalyst watches on Legrand and Halma. We recommend a barbell approach, described herein.

items.title: North America Trucking: Quality Deserves a Fresh Look
items.summary: We're upgrading ODFL and CHRW to Buy following recent pullbacks, as the risk-reward has become more reasonable and both are the leaders in their respective sub-sectors, offering an opportunity to buy quality at a reasonable price. We offer further analysis in this note.

items.title: U.S. Biotechnology & Pharmaceuticals: Fall Biopharma Outlook
items.summary: We remain optimistic that Biopharma momentum can continue through the fall. Overall, we remain most comfortable with companies capable of driving volume-led growth without relying on pricing actions, particularly where we see factors at work that can sustain momentum into 2027.

items.title: VW Is Protecting the Downside
items.summary: We offer key takeaways from VW's new cost restructuring plans. It's taken a view of future earnings downside risks and is managing forward five years, formulating a cost plan to offset this risk. Operating conditions remain very tough, but we see VW's future as far more secure than it was.

items.title: A Look at Potential Impacts of bp's Brazil Opportunity
items.summary: Several European IOCs' market valuations have been weighed down by low SEC reserve life. We see bp as alone in having an organic pathway to closing the reserve gap, much of it driven by its opportunity in Brazil. We look at the potential impacts of success with the Bumerangue field.

items.title: We're Upgrading Keyence to Buy
items.summary: We're upgrading Keyence to Buy, as its late-cycle characteristics should allow its earnings to outpace those of other factory-automation names. Higher rates are a concern, but a cash-rich balance sheet provides a cushion and the option of increasing shareholder returns, including buybacks.

items.title: European Economics: Remarkable Endurance Likely to Continue
items.summary: The euro zone's economy continues to grow slowly but steadily despite numerous exogenous shocks. We expect it to also look through the latest spike in gas prices and rising bond yields. We see GDP growth as close to 1% this year and accelerating to 1.5% in 2027.

items.title: China Property: Selling What is Built
items.summary: We expect the China Property sector to be volatile as corporates and investors digest the long-term implications of China's "completed-home sales" policy. We think reform will ultimately benefit sector leaders and would see any September pullback as a potential October buying opportunity.

items.title: World Radar Screen: September Update
items.summary: The MSCI World Value-Momentum strategy declined 3.3% in August as developed markets continued to lag their emerging-markets counterparts. EM (+2.6%) and Asia ex Japan (+3.3%) remained the clear areas of strength, extending their recent leadership and materially outperforming DM strategies.
